Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection with a complaint of left wrist pain and limited grip. Over
three visits, the patient was evaluated, imaged, and managed for a distal radius fracture. Radiographs and the physical
examination clearly confirmed the fracture, with localized swelling, tenderness over the distal radius, and reduced range of
motion at the wrist. The injury pattern is consistent with the mechanism described, namely a fall onto an outstretched hand and
forceful bracing against the vehicle interior during the impact. The patient reports no prior injury or treatment involving this wrist
or adjacent body region, and none appears in the available history. Care followed a typical course: immobilization, pain
management, and a graded return to activity with hand therapy guidance. Symptoms and functional limitations steadily improved,
and follow-up visits were tapered as healing progressed. Billed services corresponded to the visits documented, with no repeated
or duplicate charges identified.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
